body.en: Domain Restrictions, Invertibility & Asymptotic Behavior: An algebraic or transcendental function \(f: D \to R\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}: R \to D\) if and only if \(f\) is strictly one-to-one (bijective) on \(D\), guaranteeing that \(\text{dom}(f^{-1}) = \text{ran}(f)\) and \(\text{ran}(f^{-1}) = \text{dom}(f)\). For logarithmic and radical equations, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the solution set, requiring a final domain check against the original equation.
body.ar: Domain Restrictions, Invertibility & Asymptotic Behavior: An algebraic or transcendental الدالة \(f: D \to R\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}: R \to D\) if and only if \(f\) is strictly one-to-one (bijective) on \(D\), guaranteeing that \(\text{dom}(f^{-1}) = \text{ran}(f)\) and \(\text{ran}(f^{-1}) = \text{dom}(f)\). For logarithmic and radical المعادلات, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the الحل set, requiring a final المجال check against the original المعادلة.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Exponentials & Logarithms)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Exponentials & Logarithms)

body.en:
Why Completing the Square & Log-Linearization Work: Any quadratic \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) (\(a \ne 0\)) can be rewritten by factoring \(a\) from the first two terms and adding/subtracting \((b/2a)^2\):

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the range to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the المدى to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

body.en:
Problem (Medium): Find the set of all real solutions to the equation \[ \log_2(x - 1) - \log_4(x + 14) = 1 \]

Step-by-Step Solution: To solve the equation, we first express all logarithms in the same base using the change of base formula: \[ \log_4(x + 14) = \frac{\log_2(x + 14)}{\log_2 4} = \frac{\log_2(x + 14)}{2} = \frac{1}{2}\log_2(x + 14) \] Substitute this back into the original equation: \[ \log_2(x - 1) - \frac{1}{2}\log_2(x + 14) = 1 \] Multiply through by \( 2 \): \[ 2\log_2(x - 1) - \log_2(x + 14) = 2 \] Apply the power law and the quotient law of logarithms: \[ \log_2\left((x - 1)^2\right) - \log_2(x + 14) = 2 \implies \log_2\left(\frac{(x - 1)^2}{x + 14}\right) = 2 \] Convert from logarithmic form to exponential form: \[ \frac{(x - 1)^2}{x + 14} = 2^2 = 4 \] Clear the denominator and expand: \[ (x - 1)^2 = 4(x + 14) \] \[ x^2 - 2x + 1 = 4x + 56 \] \[ x^2 - 6x - 55 = 0 \] Factor the quadratic equation: \[ (x - 11)(x + 5) = 0 \implies x = 11 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -5 \] Now, we must consider the domain of the original logarithmic expressions: - For \( \log_2(x - 1) \) to be defined, \( x - 1 > 0 \implies x > 1 \). - For \( \log_4(x + 14) \) to be defined, \( x + 14 > 0 \implies x > -14 \). Thus, the domain requires \( x > 1 \). - For \( x = -5 \), the term \( \log_2(-5 - 1) = \log_2(-6) \) is undefined in the real numbers. Hence, \( x = -5 \) is an extraneous solution introduced by squaring. - For \( x = 11 \), \( \log_2(10) - \log_4(25) = \log_2(10) - \log_2(5) = \log_2(2) = 1 \), which is valid. Therefore, the only real solution is \( x = 11 \). Misconception Traps: - Choice B includes the extraneous root \( x = -5 \), failing to verify the domain requirement \( x > 1 \). - Choice C arises from an incorrect factorization of the quadratic (e.g., confusing signs as \( (x + 11)(x - 5) = 0 \)). - Choice D arises from failing to change the base of \( \log_4 \) and solving \( \frac{x + 14}{x - 1} = 2 \).
body.ar:
Problem (Medium): أوجد set of all real الحلول to the المعادلة \[ \log_2(x - 1) - \log_4(x + 14) = 1 \]

Step-by-Step الحل: To حل المعادلة, we first express all logarithms in the same base using the change of base الصيغة: \[ \log_4(x + 14) = \frac{\log_2(x + 14)}{\log_2 4} = \frac{\log_2(x + 14)}{2} = \frac{1}{2}\log_2(x + 14) \] عوّض this back into the original المعادلة: \[ \log_2(x - 1) - \frac{1}{2}\log_2(x + 14) = 1 \] Multiply through by \( 2 \): \[ 2\log_2(x - 1) - \log_2(x + 14) = 2 \] Apply the power law and the quotient law of logarithms: \[ \log_2\left((x - 1)^2\right) - \log_2(x + 14) = 2 \implies \log_2\left(\frac{(x - 1)^2}{x + 14}\right) = 2 \] Convert from logarithmic form to exponential form: \[ \frac{(x - 1)^2}{x + 14} = 2^2 = 4 \] Clear the denominator and expand: \[ (x - 1)^2 = 4(x + 14) \] \[ x^2 - 2x + 1 = 4x + 56 \] \[ x^2 - 6x - 55 = 0 \] Factor the المعادلة التربيعية: \[ (x - 11)(x + 5) = 0 \implies x = 11 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -5 \] Now, we must consider the المجال of the original logarithmic expressions: - For \( \log_2(x - 1) \) to be defined, \( x - 1 > 0 \implies x > 1 \). - For \( \log_4(x + 14) \) to be defined, \( x + 14 > 0 \implies x > -14 \). وعليه, the المجال requires \( x > 1 \). - For \( x = -5 \), the term \( \log_2(-5 - 1) = \log_2(-6) \) is undefined in the real numbers. ومنه, \( x = -5 \) is an extraneous الحل introduced by squaring. - For \( x = 11 \), \( \log_2(10) - \log_4(25) = \log_2(10) - \log_2(5) = \log_2(2) = 1 \), which is valid. وبالتالي, the only real الحل is \( x = 11 \). Misconception Traps: - Choice B includes the extraneous root \( x = -5 \), failing to verify the المجال requirement \( x > 1 \). - Choice C arises from an incorrect factorization of the quadratic (e.g., confusing signs as \( (x + 11)(x - 5) = 0 \)). - Choice D arises from failing to change the base of \( \log_4 \) and solving \( \frac{x + 14}{x - 1} = 2 \).

body.en:
Problem (Hard): Referring to the coordinate curve shown in the diagram, determine the complete set of real values of the constant \(k\) for which the equation \[ e^x - kx^2 = 0 \] has exactly three distinct real roots.

Step-by-Step Solution: First, note that \(x = 0\) is not a solution to \(e^x - kx^2 = 0\) since \(e^0 = 1 \neq 0\). Therefore, we can rewrite the equation as: \[ k = \frac{e^x}{x^2} \] Let \(f(x) = \dfrac{e^x}{x^2}\) defined for all \(x \neq 0\). The number of distinct real roots corresponds to the number of points of intersection between the curve \(y = f(x)\) and the horizontal line \(y = k\). Differentiating \(f(x)\) using the quotient rule: \[ f'(x) = \frac{e^x \cdot x^2 - e^x \cdot 2x}{x^4} = \frac{e^x x(x - 2)}{x^4} = \frac{e^x(x - 2)}{x^3} \] Setting \(f'(x) = 0\) yields the single stationary point at \(x = 2\), where: \[ f(2) = \frac{e^2}{2^2} = \frac{e^2}{4} \] Now consider the behavior of \(f(x)\) on each separate branch of its domain: 1. On the interval \((-\infty, 0)\): Both \((x - 2) < 0\) and \(x^3 < 0\), which means \(f'(x) = \frac{e^x(x - 2)}{x^3} > 0\). Thus, \(f(x)\) is strictly increasing. As \(x \to -\infty\), \(f(x) \to 0^+\), and as \(x \to 0^-\), \(f(x) \to +\infty\). By the Intermediate Value Theorem, for any \(k > 0\), the line \(y = k\) intersects this branch exactly once. 2. On the interval \((0, \infty)\): For \(0 < x < 2\), \(x - 2 < 0\) and \(x^3 > 0\), so \(f'(x) < 0\) (strictly decreasing from \(+\infty\) to \(\frac{e^2}{4}\)). For \(x > 2\), \(x - 2 > 0\) and \(x^3 > 0\), so \(f'(x) > 0\) (strictly increasing from \(\frac{e^2}{4}\) to \(+\infty\)). Hence, \(f(2) = \frac{e^2}{4}\) is a local (and global positive) minimum on \((0, \infty)\). - If \(k < \frac{e^2}{4}\), there are no intersections on \((0, \infty)\). - If \(k = \frac{e^2}{4}\), there is exactly one intersection at \(x = 2\). - If \(k > \frac{e^2}{4}\), there are exactly two distinct intersections on \((0, \infty)\). Combining both intervals: - For \(k \le 0\), there are 0 real roots since \(f(x) > 0\) everywhere. - For \(0 < k < \frac{e^2}{4}\), there is 1 negative root and 0 positive roots (1 total). - For \(k = \frac{e^2}{4}\), there is 1 negative root and 1 positive root (2 total). - For \(k > \frac{e^2}{4}\), there is 1 negative root and 2 positive roots (3 distinct real roots in total). Thus, the equation has exactly three distinct real roots if and only if \(k > \dfrac{e^2}{4}\).
body.ar:
Problem (Hard): Referring to the الإحداثي curve shown in the المخطط, حدّد complete set of real values of the الثابت \(k\) for which the المعادلة \[ e^x - kx^2 = 0 \] has exactly three distinct real roots.

Step-by-Step الحل: First, note that \(x = 0\) is not a الحل to \(e^x - kx^2 = 0\) since \(e^0 = 1 \neq 0\). وبالتالي, we can rewrite the المعادلة as: \[ k = \frac{e^x}{x^2} \] Let \(f(x) = \dfrac{e^x}{x^2}\) defined for all \(x \neq 0\). The number of distinct real roots corresponds to the number of points of التقاطع between the curve \(y = f(x)\) and the horizontal line \(y = k\). Differentiating \(f(x)\) using the quotient rule: \[ f'(x) = \frac{e^x \cdot x^2 - e^x \cdot 2x}{x^4} = \frac{e^x x(x - 2)}{x^4} = \frac{e^x(x - 2)}{x^3} \] Setting \(f'(x) = 0\) yields the single stationary point at \(x = 2\), حيث: \[ f(2) = \frac{e^2}{2^2} = \frac{e^2}{4} \] Now consider the behavior of \(f(x)\) on each separate branch of its المجال: 1. On the interval \((-\infty, 0)\): Both \((x - 2) < 0\) and \(x^3 < 0\), which means \(f'(x) = \frac{e^x(x - 2)}{x^3} > 0\). وعليه, \(f(x)\) is strictly increasing. As \(x \to -\infty\), \(f(x) \to 0^+\), and as \(x \to 0^-\), \(f(x) \to +\infty\). By the Intermediate Value مبرهنة, for any \(k > 0\), the line \(y = k\) intersects this branch exactly once. 2. On the interval \((0, \infty)\): For \(0 < x < 2\), \(x - 2 < 0\) and \(x^3 > 0\), so \(f'(x) < 0\) (strictly decreasing from \(+\infty\) to \(\frac{e^2}{4}\)). For \(x > 2\), \(x - 2 > 0\) and \(x^3 > 0\), so \(f'(x) > 0\) (strictly increasing from \(\frac{e^2}{4}\) to \(+\infty\)). ومنه, \(f(2) = \frac{e^2}{4}\) is a local (and global positive) minimum on \((0, \infty)\). - If \(k < \frac{e^2}{4}\), there are no intersections on \((0, \infty)\). - If \(k = \frac{e^2}{4}\), there is exactly one التقاطع at \(x = 2\). - If \(k > \frac{e^2}{4}\), there are exactly two distinct intersections on \((0, \infty)\). Combining both intervals: - For \(k \le 0\), there are 0 real roots since \(f(x) > 0\) everywhere. - For \(0 < k < \frac{e^2}{4}\), there is 1 negative root and 0 positive roots (1 total). - For \(k = \frac{e^2}{4}\), there is 1 negative root and 1 positive root (2 total). - For \(k > \frac{e^2}{4}\), there is 1 negative root and 2 positive roots (3 distinct real roots in total). وعليه, the المعادلة has exactly three distinct real roots if and only if \(k > \dfrac{e^2}{4}\).

label.en: ⚠️ Cambridge 9709 Traps — Linear Reduction of Non-linear Laws
label.ar: ⚠️ Cambridge 9709 Traps — Linear Reduction of Non-linear Laws (الدوال الأسية واللوغاريتمية)

body.en:
A classic Cambridge P3 question asks students to reduce experimental data to a straight line \(Y = mX + c\). Be certain of the form:

  • Exponential form \(y = Ab^x\): Take logs: \(\ln y = x\ln b + \ln A\). Plot \(\ln y\) against \(x\). The gradient is \(\ln b\) (so \(b = e^m\)) and vertical intercept is \(\ln A\) (so \(A = e^c\)).
  • Power form \(y = Ax^n\): Take logs: \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln A\). Plot \(\ln y\) against \(\ln x\). The gradient is the exponent \(n\) directly, and the vertical intercept is \(\ln A\).

A fatal mistake is forgetting that the constant \(A\) is \(e^{\text{intercept}}\), not the intercept itself!

question.en: Variables \(x\) and \(y\) satisfy \(y = a x^b\). A graph of \(\ln y\) against \(\ln x\) is a straight line passing through \((0, 1.20)\) and \((4, 6.80)\). Find the values of the constants \(a\) and \(b\) to 3 significant figures.
question.ar: Variables \(x\) and \(y\) satisfy \(y = a x^b\). A graph of \(\ln y\) against \(\ln x\) is a straight line passing through \((0, 1.20)\) and \((4, 6.80)\). أوجد values of the constants \(a\) and \(b\) to 3 signإذا كانicant figures.

solution.en:
Take natural logarithms of \(y = a x^b\):

\[\ln y = \ln a + b\ln x\]

This is a linear equation \(Y = mX + c\) with \(Y = \ln y\), \(X = \ln x\), gradient \(m = b\), and intercept \(c = \ln a\).

Gradient:

\[b = \frac{6.80 - 1.20}{4 - 0} = \frac{5.60}{4} = 1.40\]

Vertical intercept gives \(\ln a = 1.20\):

\[a = e^{1.20} \approx 3.32\]

Therefore, \(a = 3.32\) and \(b = 1.40\).

question.ar: [Practice 3 · Easy] أوجد exact real solution to the equation \[ 2e^{2x} + 5e^x - 12 = 0. \]

hints.en: We recognize that the equation is quadratic in terms of \( e^x \): \(2(e^x)^2 + 5(e^x) - 12 = 0\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( e^x \) ، \(2(e^x)^2 + 5(e^x) - 12 = 0\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Let \( u = e^x \). Then the equation becomes: \(2u^2 + 5u - 12 = 0\) Factoring the quadratic expression: \((2u - 3)(u + 4) = 0\).
hints.ar: ليكن \( u = e^x \). Then the equation becomes: \(2u^2 + 5u - 12 = 0\) حلّلing the quadratic expression: \((2u - 3)(u + 4) = 0\).

hints.en: Thus, the only real solution is \(x = \ln\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)\).
hints.ar: وعليه، the only real solution is \(x = \ln\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)\).

solution.en:
We recognize that the equation is quadratic in terms of \( e^x \):
\[ 2(e^x)^2 + 5(e^x) - 12 = 0. \]

Let \( u = e^x \). Then the equation becomes:
\[ 2u^2 + 5u - 12 = 0. \]

Factoring the quadratic expression:
\[ (2u - 3)(u + 4) = 0. \]

This gives two possible values for \( u \):
\[ u = \frac{3}{2} \quad \text{or} \quad u = -4. \]

Since \( u = e^x \):
1. For \( e^x = \frac{3}{2} \), taking the natural logarithm of both sides yields:
\[ x = \ln\left(\frac{3}{2}\right). \]

2. For \( e^x = -4 \), since \( e^x > 0 \) for all real numbers \( x \), there are no real solutions.

Thus, the only real solution is \( x = \ln\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) \).

Common errors include:
- Factoring with incorrect signs as \( (2u + 3)(u - 4) = 0 \), which leads to the incorrect root \( x = \ln 4 \).
- Forgetting to take the logarithm of \( u \), giving \( x = \frac{3}{2} \).
- Failing to discard the negative root \( u = -4 \) and falsely combining signs.

label.en: ● Master Atlas of the 9 Main Parent Functions & Universal Transformation Law
label.ar: ● الأطلس الشامل للدوال الأم التسع وقانون التحويلات الهندسية العام

body.en:
Every algebraic and elementary transcendental model is built by transforming one of the nine core parent functions via \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\), where \(|a|\) scales vertically (reflecting across the \(x\)-axis if \(a < 0\)), \(h\) shifts horizontally, and \(k\) shifts vertically:

FamilyTransformed Form \(g(x)\)DomainRange (\(a > 0\))Key Geometric Feature
Constant\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)Horizontal line, slope \(0\)
Linear\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Constant slope \(m = a\), pivot \((h, k)\)
Quadratic\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Parabola vertex \((h, k)\), axis \(x = h\)
Cubic\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Inflection center \((h, k)\), S-curve
Absolute Value\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)V-corner vertex \((h, k)\), slopes \(\pm a\)
Radical\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Endpoint \((h, k)\), half-parabola
Rational\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), horizontal \(y = k\)
Exponential\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)Horizontal asymptote \(y = k\), anchor \((h, a+k)\)
Logarithmic\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), anchor \((h+1, k)\)
body.ar:
تُبنى النماذج الجبرية والمتسامية الأساسية من خلال تطبيق التحويل القياسي \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\) على إحدى الدوال الأم التسع، حيث يتحكم \(|a|\) في التمدد الرأسي (مع انعكاس حول محور السينات إذا كان \(a < 0\))، ويمثل \(h\) الإزاحة الأفقية، و\(k\) الإزاحة الرأسية:

عائلة الدالةالصورة المحوّلة \(g(x)\)المجالالمدى (\(a > 0\))السمة الهندسية المميزة
الثابتة\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)مستقيم أفقي ميله \(0\)
الخطية\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)ميل ثابت \(m = a\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h, k)\)
التربيعية\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)قطع مكافئ رأسه \((h, k)\) ومحوره \(x = h\)
التكعيبية\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)نقطة انعطاف مركزية \((h, k)\)
القيمة المطلقة\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)رأس زاوي على شكل V عند \((h, k)\) بميلين \(\pm a\)
الجذرية\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)نقطة بداية \((h, k)\) ومجال مقيّد \(x \ge h\)
النسبية (المقلوب)\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)تقارب رأسي \(x = h\) وتقارب أفقي \(y = k\)
الأسية\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)تقارب أفقي \(y = k\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h, a+k)\)
اللوغاريتمية\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)تقارب رأسي \(x = h\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h+1, k)\)

label.en: ● Hyperbolic & Inverse Hyperbolic Functions in Calculus — Definitions, Identities & Derivatives
label.ar: ● الدوال الزائدية وعكسها في التفاضل والتكامل — التعاريف والمتطابقات والمشتقات

body.en:
Just as circular trigonometric functions parameterize the unit circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\), the six hyperbolic functions parameterize the right branch of the unit hyperbola \(x^2 - y^2 = 1\) using combinations of \(e^x\) and \(e^{-x}\):

\[ \sinh x = rac{e^x - e^{-x}}{2}, \qquad \cosh x = rac{e^x + e^{-x}}{2}, \qquad anh x = rac{\sinh x}{\cosh x} = rac{e^x - e^{-x}}{e^x + e^{-x}} \]\[ \operatorname{csch} x = rac{1}{\sinh x}\;(x eq 0), \qquad \operatorname{sech} x = rac{1}{\cosh x}, \qquad \coth x = rac{\cosh x}{\sinh x}\;(x eq 0) \]
FunctionDomain & RangeDerivative \( rac{d}{dx}\)Logarithmic Inverse & Derivative
\(\sinh x\)Dom \(\mathbb{R}\), Rng \(\mathbb{R}\)\(\cosh x\)\(\operatorname{arsinh} x = \ln\! ig(x + \sqrt{x^2+1} ig)\), \( rac{1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}\)
\(\cosh x\)Dom \(\mathbb{R}\), Rng \([1, \infty)\)\(\sinh x\)\(\operatorname{arcosh} x = \ln\! ig(x + \sqrt{x^2-1} ig)\;(x\ge 1)\), \( rac{1}{\sqrt{x^2-1}}\)
\( anh x\)Dom \(\mathbb{R}\), Rng \((-1, 1)\)\(\operatorname{sech}^2 x\)\(\operatorname{artanh} x = rac{1}{2}\ln\!\left( rac{1+x}{1-x} ight)\;(|x|<1)\), \( rac{1}{1-x^2}\)
\(\operatorname{csch} x\)Dom \(x eq 0\), Rng \(y eq 0\)\(-\operatorname{csch} x\coth x\)Odd reciprocal of \(\sinh x\)
\(\operatorname{sech} x\)Dom \(\mathbb{R}\), Rng \((0, 1]\)\(-\operatorname{sech} x anh x\)Bell-shaped reciprocal of \(\cosh x\)
\(\coth x\)Dom \(x eq 0\), Rng \(|y|>1\)\(-\operatorname{csch}^2 x\)Horizontal asymptotes \(y = \pm 1\)

Fundamental Hyperbolic Identity: \(\cosh^2 x - \sinh^2 x = 1\), \(1 - anh^2 x = \operatorname{sech}^2 x\), and \(\sinh(2x) = 2\sinh x\cosh x\). Physically, a flexible uniform cable hanging under gravity forms the catenary curve \(y = a\cosh(x/a)\).
body.ar:
كما تُمثّل الدوال المثلثية الدائرية دائرة الوحدة \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\)، فإن الدوال الزائدية الست تُوسِّط الفرع الأيمن للقطع الزائد الواحدي \(x^2 - y^2 = 1\) بدلالة الدالتين الأسيتين \(e^x\) و\(e^{-x}\):

\[ \sinh x = rac{e^x - e^{-x}}{2}, \qquad \cosh x = rac{e^x + e^{-x}}{2}, \qquad anh x = rac{\sinh x}{\cosh x} = rac{e^x - e^{-x}}{e^x + e^{-x}} \]\[ \operatorname{csch} x = rac{1}{\sinh x}\;(x eq 0), \qquad \operatorname{sech} x = rac{1}{\cosh x}, \qquad \coth x = rac{\cosh x}{\sinh x}\;(x eq 0) \]
الدالةالمجال والمدىالمشتقة \( rac{d}{dx}\)الصيغة اللوغاريتمية للعكس ومشتقتها
\(\sinh x\)المجال \(\mathbb{R}\)، المدى \(\mathbb{R}\)\(\cosh x\)\(\operatorname{arsinh} x = \ln\! ig(x + \sqrt{x^2+1} ig)\)، \( rac{1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}\)
\(\cosh x\)المجال \(\mathbb{R}\)، المدى \([1, \infty)\)\(\sinh x\)\(\operatorname{arcosh} x = \ln\! ig(x + \sqrt{x^2-1} ig)\;(x\ge 1)\)، \( rac{1}{\sqrt{x^2-1}}\)
\( anh x\)المجال \(\mathbb{R}\)، المدى \((-1, 1)\)\(\operatorname{sech}^2 x\)\(\operatorname{artanh} x = rac{1}{2}\ln\!\left( rac{1+x}{1-x} ight)\;(|x|<1)\)، \( rac{1}{1-x^2}\)
\(\operatorname{csch} x\)المجال \(x eq 0\)، المدى \(y eq 0\)\(-\operatorname{csch} x\coth x\)دالة فردية مقلوبة لـ \(\sinh x\)
\(\operatorname{sech} x\)المجال \(\mathbb{R}\)، المدى \((0, 1]\)\(-\operatorname{sech} x anh x\)منحنى جرسي متماثل مقلوب لـ \(\cosh x\)
\(\coth x\)المجال \(x eq 0\)، المدى \(|y|>1\)\(-\operatorname{csch}^2 x\)خطا تقارب أفقيان \(y = \pm 1\)

المتطابقة الزائدية الأساسية: \(\cosh^2 x - \sinh^2 x = 1\)، و\(1 - anh^2 x = \operatorname{sech}^2 x\)، و\(\sinh(2x) = 2\sinh x\cosh x\). فيزيائياً، يتخذ الكابل المتجانس المعلّق تحت تأثير الجاذبية شكل منحنى السلسلة \(y = a\cosh(x/a)\).
